battery.title: Battery
battery.description:
Used to plan when buying cheap and selling dear pays off, using your buy and sell prices.

A kWh sold must have been bought for less than: *sell price − degradation cost*, multiplied by the efficiency.

**Your real battery (optional):** pick a state-of-charge sensor (%, Wh or kWh) so today's plan starts from what is actually stored, and optionally a capacity sensor (Wh or kWh) to replace the fixed capacity below. Without them the plan assumes an empty battery.

data.battery_usable_pct: Share of the battery to use

data_description.battery_charge_power_kw: Most power the battery can draw from the grid, in kW at the grid side. 300 W = 0.3 kW.
data_description.battery_discharge_power_kw: Most power it can deliver to the grid, in kW. 1200 W = 1.2 kW. Charging and discharging limits are often different.
data_description.battery_round_trip_efficiency_pct: Share of grid energy that comes back out: buy → store → sell. 85-95% is typical for lithium batteries.
data_description.battery_degradation_per_kwh: Battery wear per kWh delivered, in {currency}. Roughly battery price per kWh ÷ lifetime cycles (e.g. 1500 ÷ 6000 = 0.25).
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Percent, Wh or kWh. Used for today's plan.
data_description.battery_capacity_entity: Usable capacity in Wh or kWh. Replaces the fixed capacity.
data_description.battery_usable_pct: The planner only works with this share of the capacity. The rest is a reserve at the bottom that is never sold (backup power, your own use). 50% of a 10 kWh battery means 5 kWh to plan with and 5 kWh kept.

source_entity.title: Price sensor
source_entity.description: Pick the sensor that provides the prices. It must have a `prices` attribute with `start`, `end`, `buy` and `sell` for each interval (per kWh), like the *Upcoming prices* sensor of the OPCOM PZU integration. Prices must already include what you pay and receive (taxes, VAT, commission).

data_description.price_entity: Needs a `prices` attribute; see the documentation for the format.

source_fixed.title: Fixed prices
source_fixed.description:
For a fixed tariff. Prices per kWh in {currency}, with taxes, network charges and VAT included, as on your bill.

Optionally add a **second rate** for some hours, for example a night rate. It applies from the start time to the end time (it may run past midnight) on the days you pick. Leave it empty if you have one price.

data_description.fixed_buy_price: What you pay for a kWh from the grid.
data_description.fixed_sell_price: What you receive for a kWh sent to the grid. 0 if you are not paid for it.
data_description.rate2_days: The day an interval falls on decides it.

error.no_prices: That sensor has no usable `prices` attribute. Pick a sensor that follows the price series format.
error.rate2_incomplete: The second rate needs all four of its fields: from, until, buy price and sell price. Fill them all or clear them.
error.rate2_same_time: The second rate starts and ends at the same time. Give it a different end.

consumption.title: House consumption
consumption.description:
So the planner can learn how much your house uses and when. Everything is optional.

**Pick one way to measure the house:**
- a sensor that measures the house directly, **or**
- **one grid power sensor** that is positive when importing and negative when exporting (tick *flip* if yours is the other way round), **or**
- **two grid sensors**, one for import and one for export, both positive.

With a grid sensor you can add your **solar production** and **battery power** (positive = charging), so energy that goes into the battery or comes from the sun is not counted as house use. Sensors must be in W or kW. The pattern is learned from Home Assistant's long-term statistics of these sensors, which need `state_class: measurement` (most power sensors have it), per hour, separately for weekdays and weekends. An **EV charger** can be taken out, as it is a large and unpredictable load.

**Solar forecast:** if your Energy dashboard has solar forecasts (Forecast.Solar, Solcast, Open-Meteo and others), they are used automatically, all of them added up. In the *Balanced* and *Cheap self-consumption* modes the plan then stores the sun instead of exporting it when the price is low.

data.grid_power_flip: Grid sensor reports export as positive
data.battery_power_flip: Battery sensor reports discharging as positive
data.ev_takes_surplus: The car follows the solar surplus
data.ev_battery_trickle_kw: Car: what the battery still gets

data_description.house_power_entity: Use this if one sensor already tells the house's power. The others are then ignored.
data_description.grid_power_entity: Positive when importing from the grid, negative when exporting.
data_description.grid_import_entity: Power drawn from the grid, always positive.
data_description.grid_export_entity: Power sent to the grid, always positive.
data_description.solar_power_entity: One or several sensors in W or kW; they are added up. Used to work out the house's consumption and to follow what the panels make now.
data_description.battery_power_entity: Positive while charging, negative while discharging.
data_description.ev_power_entity: Left out of the house's consumption: an EV is a big, unpredictable load that is rarely charged from the home battery.
data_description.ev_takes_surplus: For an EV charger that charges from solar surplus. The plan then expects the car to take part of the sun before the battery does, as often as it did in the past. Needs the EV sensor, a solar sensor and a few weeks of history.
data_description.ev_start_surplus_kw: The surplus (sun minus the house) at which the charger starts, in kW.
data_description.ev_max_power_kw: The most the charger can draw, in kW.
data_description.ev_battery_trickle_kw: While the car charges, the battery still gets about this much of the surplus, in kW. 1 kW is typical.

error.no_prices: That sensor has no usable `prices` attribute. Pick a sensor that follows the price series format.
error.grid_both: Use either one grid power sensor or the import and export pair, not both.
error.grid_pair: The import and export sensors go together: pick both or neither.
error.grid_missing: Solar and battery power only help together with a grid sensor (or the import and export pair).
